study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Italinna et al., PLoS Comput Biol, 2023
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Using normative modeling and machine learning for detecting mild traumatic brain injury from magnetoencephalography data

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Normative model is constructed by computing mean and standard deviation across the reference dataset (z-scoring); no specific normative modeling algorithm from the list is reported.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To obtain normative models, the mean μ and standard deviation σ of the power spectra were calculated across the subjects from the normative dataset (Fig 1B).

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Source-level MEG power spectral densities across cortical locations.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: An automated source-modeling pipeline was applied on the measurements to compute power spectral densities (PSDs) at each cortical location

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: No covariates reported; normative model uses reference-sample mean and standard deviation only.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: To obtain normative models, the mean μ and standard deviation σ of the power spectra were calculated across the subjects from the normative dataset (Fig 1B).
